identifying_c.definition_route: For U1 define a model parameter c:=|L|/tau explicitly; for N1 use index-dependent c_n if desired. These definitions label selected conditional ratios, not derive or measure a pre-existing propagation constant.
identifying_c.evidence_route: If c denotes a specified physical propagation speed, supply its meaning, a physical event interpretation, calibrated length and time scales, and independent evidence or a governing relation showing that this process has that propagation speed.
identifying_c.circularity: Choosing tau=|L|/c from a preselected positive c imposes the ratio when |L|>0. It cannot derive c from the source. At L=0 that positive-clock construction does not apply.
identifying_c.assigned_evidence: None of those identifying physical inputs is supplied in the frozen packet.
identifying_c.nonlinear_boundary: For nonzero L and fixed tau>0, N1 cannot equal one fixed positive c at all intervals. One may define c_n:=|L|/[tau(2n+1)], explicitly an index-dependent model parameter. Matching one selected interval by choosing tau=|L|/[c(2n+1)] imposes that interval value; it does not derive a physical c or a global constant.

limits: tau=0 makes the quotient undefined; tau>0 is explicitly proposed.

For nonzero L, varying proposed tau changes the ratio without changing any source position. Parameter limits tau toward zero or infinity are mathematical limits, not physically achievable speed evidence.
If L=0, sampled positions coincide. A time map and physical interpretation remain unassigned; no physical propagation constant is identified.
Unequal positive clock intervals give v_n=L/[t(n+1)-t(n)]. The source does not establish a uniform interval speed.
A discrete interval quotient does not establish instantaneous motion between indices without additional interpolation or dynamics.
No external research, experiment, validated physics or Aether-Flow result is supplied or claimed.
N1 and U1 are competing optional clock hypotheses. For nonzero L they agree on the n=0 step interval but predict different later ratios; neither can be presented as the unique source-assigned clock.
The nonzero sampled nonlinear interval at n=0 is tau; a continuous derivative of a speculative interpolation is not the discrete denominator.
